entries.name: Send to a channel
entries.summary: Post a message into a chat channel as the user, straight from the composer.
entries.narrative: A composer verb in the no-UI shell. /send #channel <text> posts the text into that channel AS THE USER, so everyone in the channel sees it under their name. It is risky because it speaks for the user in front of others and a sent message cannot be unsent from the composer. Suggest it when the user wants to say something in a channel without opening the chat; to read a channel instead, use the read-only room tools.
entries.how: type /send #channel your message in the composer

entries.name: New task
entries.summary: Create a task from the composer, optionally assigned to a teammate with @name.
entries.narrative: A composer verb in the no-UI shell. /task <title> @person creates a task (the alias /new-task does the same). Mention a teammate to assign it. Suggest it when the user wants a to-do recorded or handed to someone, e.g. 'you can also type /task Fix login @rohit'.
entries.how: type /task Fix login @rohit in the composer (alias /new-task)

entries.name: Build a site
entries.summary: Ask the agent to build a website from a one-line brief, from the composer.
entries.narrative: A composer verb in the no-UI shell. /site <brief> hands the brief to the agent, which builds a Paw Site draft (a Pocket that can be published). Use it as the fast path for 'make me a site for ...'; publishing stays a separate, explicit step.
entries.how: type /site a calm dentist landing page in the composer

entries.name: Catch me up
entries.summary: One-tap room summary: the agent reads the room's recent messages and sums them up.
entries.narrative: A composer verb in the no-UI shell. The room's 'Catch me up' action sends the room's recent messages to the agent, which summarizes them. Read-only: nothing is posted. The agent side of this is the read-only room tools.
entries.how: the 'Catch me up' action on a room
